proposal: The Mandate recommends that Healthy Marriage and Responsible Fatherhood funds support national messaging campaigns affirming fathers' roles, and that grant allocations protect and prioritize faith-based programs that involve churches and mentorship and teach fatherhood on a biological and sociological basis rather than as a gender-neutral parent role (pp. 481 to 482).

source_checks.note: Checked 2026-10-15: posted 2025-07-15, $55 million, 66 awards; equal treatment of faith-based applicants; fathers or father figures; no messaging campaign mentioned.
Checked 2026-10-15: Ad Council fatherhood PSA page sponsored by the National Responsible Fatherhood Clearinghouse and ACF; no release date shown, so it cannot be placed after 2025-01-20; not cited.

Federal Register API, term fatherhood, HHS, since 2025-01-20: 5 documents, all HMRF information-collection notices (2026-01-29, 2026-05-04), an ACF research collection (2026-08-05), a delegations notice (2025-12-19) and a Medicare rule; none sets a messaging campaign or faith-based priority.

Same pattern for ACF with term marriage: 6 documents (HMRF performance measures notices, Head Start, TANF work participation and Unaccompanied Children proposed rules); none addresses fatherhood messaging or allocation priority.

HHS rule list (183 rules, whole list read) has no title naming fatherhood, marriage or the Office of Family Assistance. Related: RIN 0991-AC44 (faith-based participation, NPRM projected 11/00/2026), which does not address HMRF. Reviewer reopened the list on 2026-10-19 and confirmed the heading and the RINs and titles named. Titles naming family are 0970-AD38 and 0970-AD42 (burden reduction), not HMRF priorities.

Domain-limited search (congress.gov, govinfo.gov) surfaced S. 2131 and H.R. 5828, Dads Matter Act of 2025, which would require HHS to run a public awareness campaign on father engagement in perinatal health. S. 2131 introduced 2025-06-18, referred to HELP; H.R. 5828 introduced 2025-10-24, referred to Energy and Commerce. Introduced bills only; not an HMRF messaging campaign. H.Res.487 (sense of the House on fatherhood) also seen.

ACF press release dated 2025-09-30: over $100 million in HMRF grants to 109 organizations in 38 states; no messaging campaign, no faith-based or biological-basis priority mentioned. ACF HMRF program page (acf.gov/ofa/programs/healthy-marriage-responsible-fatherhood) likewise mentions neither and lists the FORGE Fatherhood, HEART and READY4Life cohorts running through 2030-09-29. Reviewer reopened the release on 2026-10-19: same content.

One standard web search (HMRF national campaign, faith-based fatherhood grants, 2026) returned only grant listings and the ACF 2025 award release; no news of a national messaging campaign or faith-based allocation priority.

significance.rationale: Fatherhood messaging and faith-based grant priority.

status_summary: No new national fatherhood messaging campaign and no allocation priority for faith-based or biological-basis fatherhood programs was found since 2025-01-20. On 2025-07-15 ACF posted the FORGE Fatherhood funding opportunity (about $55 million, 66 expected awards) under the HMRF program for responsible fatherhood activities in marriage, parenting and economic stability; it treats faith-based applicants on the same basis as others and refers to fathers or father figures. That listing is a standard HMRF grant competition and does not carry a messaging campaign or the requested priority.
title: Fund a pro-fatherhood messaging campaign and prioritize faith-based fatherhood programs
uncertainties: The HHS rule list on reginfo.gov (labeled Agency Rule List - 2026) lists no rulemaking on fatherhood messaging or HMRF allocation priorities; RIN 0991-AC44 concerns faith-based participation in HHS programs generally and is a planned rule only. The FORGE Fatherhood listing (2025-07-15) treats faith-based applicants on the same basis as others and carries no messaging campaign. Ad Council fatherhood PSA pages sponsored by the National Responsible Fatherhood Clearinghouse and ACF carry no release dates, so new campaign material after 2025-01-20 is not shown. The introduced Dads Matter Act bills (S. 2131, H.R. 5828) would require a perinatal father-engagement awareness campaign and are not an HMRF action. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
